title: MCBound: An Online Framework to Characterize and Classify Memory/Compute-bound HPC Jobs
problem: HPC jobs exhibit conflicting computational requirements causing inefficiencies in resource usage, system throughput, and energy consumption. There is no existing method to classify jobs as memory-bound or compute-bound at submission time without user intervention.
motivation: Distinguishing memory-bound from compute-bound jobs enables better scheduling decisions to improve resource efficiency and reduce energy consumption in HPC systems.
method: MCBound learns from 2.2 million historical job runs on Supercomputer Fugaku, identifying which ones were limited by how fast they could move data versus how fast they could compute. It then builds machine learning models based on these patterns and uses them to predict, as you submit a new job, whether it will be bottlenecked by data movement (memory-bound) or processor speed (compute-bound). These predictions are accurate 89% of the time (F1-macro score of 0.89, a standard metric for classification accuracy), with negligible added system burden.
key_novelty: MCBound automatically predicts at submission time whether a job will be limited by data movement or computing power, learning from patterns in past runs without needing user intervention.
contributions: Online framework for automated memory/compute-bound job classification in HPC systems
Systematic characterization technique generating reference datasets from historical job data
Evaluation on 2.2 million production job runs achieving 0.89 F1-macro prediction quality
Portable Python implementation deployable across different HPC systems

metrics.accuracy: F1-macro average score of at least 0.89

primary_theme: HPC job characterization and adaptive scheduling
